subject: Cooking
title: The Michelin Star System: Tire Company to Taste Arbiter
description: A 60-second lesson on The Michelin Star System: Tire Company to Taste Arbiter.

hook.text: The world's most prestigious restaurant rating was invented to sell tires. That's not a joke.

buildup.text: In 1900, Michelin Tires published a free driving guide with gas stations, hotels, and good restaurants.

discovery.text: The logic: if people drove farther for great food, they'd wear out tires faster and buy more Michelin products.

twist.text: By 1926, they added the star system. Three stars meant 'worth a special journey' — a meaning unchanged today.

climax.text: Losing a star has driven chefs to depression and even suicide — the pressure of Michelin's power is immense.

punchline.text: The most feared critics in food are anonymous inspectors from a tire company.

quiz.question: Why did the Michelin tire company create a restaurant guide?
options: To encourage driving (and tire purchases) to distant restaurants
A chef was on the board

details.summary: The Michelin Guide began in 1900 as a free tire company promotion encouraging French motorists to drive more and wear out tires. Its star rating system, introduced in 1926, accidentally became the most powerful force in fine dining, capable of making or breaking a chef's career overnight.
details.whyItMatters: A tire company becoming the world's ultimate dining authority is one of food history's strangest stories. Understanding Michelin's origins reveals how arbitrary systems can acquire enormous cultural power.
takeaways: Michelin started as a free booklet to encourage driving and tire sales
Three stars means a restaurant is worth a special journey
Gaining or losing a star can change a restaurant's revenue by 25 percent

faq.question: How do Michelin inspectors evaluate restaurants?
faq.answer: Anonymous inspectors dine like regular customers and pay their own bills. They evaluate quality of ingredients, mastery of technique, personality of the chef in the cuisine, value for money, and consistency. Multiple inspectors visit over multiple occasions before any star decision is made.

faq.question: Has anyone rejected Michelin stars?
faq.answer: Several chefs have asked to be removed from the guide. Sébastien Bras requested removal in 2017, citing the pressure of maintaining stars. Some chefs argue the system imposes French fine dining standards on other cuisines.
